regulations.title: LCRB Manufacturer licence to produce beer, wine, or spirits
regulations.summary: Any business that makes beer, wine, or spirits in BC needs a Manufacturer licence (winery, brewery, or distillery type) from the Liquor and Cannabis Regulation Branch before production can begin, including local government or Indigenous Nation input on the application.
regulations.regulation_name: Liquor Control and Licensing Act and Regulation
regulations.action_required: Apply for the correct Manufacturer licence type through the LCRB's online liquor and cannabis licensing portal (requires a Business BCeID), including any required local government resolution.
regulations.penalty_note: Manufacturing or selling liquor without the required licence is an offence under the Liquor Control and Licensing Act, subject to fines and product seizure.
regulations.source_name: Province of British Columbia - Apply for a Manufacturer licence

regulations.title: Manufacturer sales agreement with the BC Liquor Distribution Branch
regulations.summary: Once your Manufacturer licence gets Approval in Principle, the BC Liquor Distribution Branch (the province's wholesaler) works with you to set up a manufacturer sales agreement, which governs how your product is warehoused, priced, and distributed to retailers.
regulations.action_required: Coordinate with the BC Liquor Distribution Branch to finalize a manufacturer sales agreement before your product can be sold through BC retail or hospitality channels.
regulations.penalty_note: Selling manufactured liquor outside an approved LDB sales agreement can jeopardize your Approval in Principle and licence standing.
regulations.source_name: BC Liquor Distribution Branch - Become a Manufacturer

regulations.title: Moratorium on new private liquor retail store licences
regulations.summary: BC has frozen new Licensee Retail Store (private liquor store) licences until July 1, 2032. If your plan depends on opening a new standalone retail liquor store, this is currently not possible; the only path in is converting an existing eligible wine store licence.
regulations.regulation_name: Liquor Control and Licensing Regulation - Licensee Retail Store policy
regulations.action_required: Do not plan on a new standalone BC liquor retail store licence before the moratorium lifts; consider alternative routes such as manufacturer on-site retail or licensed grocery listings instead.
regulations.penalty_note: Operating a retail liquor outlet without an issued licence is an offence under the Liquor Control and Licensing Act; applications submitted during the freeze are not accepted.
regulations.source_name: Province of British Columbia - Licensee Retail Store

regulations.title: 10% PST on liquor sales
regulations.summary: Liquor sold in BC is taxed at a special 10% Provincial Sales Tax rate rather than the standard 7% rate, and sellers must register with the Ministry of Finance to collect and remit it.
regulations.regulation_name: Provincial Sales Tax Act - liquor rate
regulations.action_required: Register for a PST number and set up billing/POS systems to charge 10% PST on all liquor sales made in BC.
regulations.penalty_note: Under-collecting or failing to remit the liquor PST rate can result in retroactive assessment plus penalties and interest.
regulations.source_name: Province of British Columbia - PST for food/beverage service providers and retail liquor sellers

regulations.title: BC business entity registration before applying for a liquor licence
regulations.summary: The LCRB requires applicants to already be a registered BC business entity (sole proprietorship, partnership, or corporation) before a liquor licence application will be accepted.
regulations.regulation_name: Business Corporations Act / Partnership Act - business registration requirements
regulations.authority: BC Registry Services, Ministry of Citizens' Services
regulations.action_required: Reserve a business name and register your sole proprietorship, partnership, or corporation with BC Registry Services before starting your liquor licence application.
regulations.penalty_note: A liquor licence application without proof of a registered BC business entity will be rejected or held incomplete.
regulations.source_name: Province of British Columbia - Sole proprietorships and partnerships
